note: Measured constants of the swarm. Exploratory (round 1b), not holdout-confirmed. Coordinator-curated from integrated reports; each value cites its hypothesis card. Update when a card changes.

constants.name: per-pair attention dilution exponent
constants.value: 0.66 ± 0.02 | CORRECTION 2026-10-04: k^−0.66 (all talk calls, D1) is not separable from reactive timing (null 0.75–0.80); the identified value is the #51 timer-wake exponent 0.45 [0.41, 0.50] (round 1b; round 1 gave 0.50)
constants.meaning: Reply rate per sender falls as k^−β with k pending senders.

constants.name: exposure-time elasticity of the reply hazard
constants.value: −0.00 ± 0.05 (G51); +0.51 [0.41, 0.61] regime I | updated 2026-10-05 (H40 round 2): base η G38 −0.57 [−0.67, −0.46], G44 −0.34 [−0.44, −0.24] is mostly call-type composition (74–81% removed by the talk split; η_talk −0.28 [−0.39, −0.18]); given a talk call η = −0.11 [−0.16, −0.06] in G38, G40, G41, G44 (τ 0); regime I: start-placement artifact +0.04 [−0.06, 0.13] (excluded), full-strength scheduler-wait exposure excluded, cause open
constants.meaning: 0 = coupling runs on the call clock; 1 = on the wall clock. | Round 2: in regimes II–III the wall clock (η = 1) is excluded everywhere; a negative total η means long tool calls are followed by fewer talk calls, not a negative wall-clock effect.

constants.name: cadence elasticity of 5-min coupling
constants.meaning: Doubling the call rate raises 5-min reply coupling by about ×1.5.

constants.name: hop-1 coupling, named vs unnamed
constants.value: 0.17 vs 0.004 | updated 2026-10-05 (H67 round 2): H50's J₁ scale is ≈ 2× g_lag through its pair-RD design (regime III: half local-linear extrapolation, half pair sampling; +0.05 to +0.07 with no coupling in synthetic worlds) and call-class composition (regime I); use H67's J₁* for magnitudes (named 0.079 [0.069, 0.089] vs unnamed 0.004, ×19)
constants.meaning: Only addressed messages couple at the first read-out. | The named/unnamed contrast stands; the absolute scale does not.

constants.name: idea branching ratio
constants.meaning: A new idea makes 0.22 new adopters per adopter; cascades die out.

constants.name: activity branching ratio (Hawkes)
constants.meaning: Activity is subcritical: most events are driven, not self-excited.

constants.name: room loop gain, content and talk
constants.value: content ≈ 0.47, talk ≈ 0.64 (30 min)
constants.meaning: Content and talk co-move inside rooms; activity has no room gain.

constants.name: schedule share of regime-III co-activation
constants.meaning: Most activity synchrony is the runner's start/stop schedule (a field).

constants.name: convergence share of exposure effects
constants.value: ≈ 1/3 (content, 60 s lag); ≈ 1/2 (ideas) | updated 2026-10-05 (H54 round 2): human messages, read vs unread in flight at matched lag × before-age: 0.48 (bge) / 0.40 (gte), no CI; (H08 round 2): for content of statements that neither name nor reply to the sender, median κ_c 1.68 over regime-III periods (bge; > 1 in 7/9), i.e. convergence explains all of it
constants.scope: in-flight placebo at matched lag | in-flight placebo at matched lag; H08's κ_c is not a pure convergence share (a shared drifting topic alone gives ≈ 0.73)
constants.meaning: Part of apparent influence happens without reading: shared fields and priors.

constants.name: median read-out delay
constants.meaning: A message acts at the recipient's next model call.

constants.name: content settling time after a kickoff
constants.value: ≈ 4.5 h (bge) / 1.9 h (gte)
constants.scope: coverage 0.24 h; about 10× slower than coverage
constants.meaning: Agents see everything in minutes but settle in hours.

constants.name: spread velocity
constants.value: 1 hop per 1.5–5 talk calls
constants.meaning: Spread is set by talk turns, not cadence or volume.

constants.name: forced-erasure work cost
constants.value: commits −39% [−42, −35] for ~10 turns; ≈ 10% of a segment; output −41% [−38, −44] over 20 calls (H87) | updated 2026-10-05 (H44 round 2): the write dip depends on the reference window: −20% (whole closed segment), −26% (far), −31% (near), −32% (agent-day steady state), −11% [−18, −4] (40-call cycle mean); cost per reset 0.19–0.59 write calls; sawtooth cost vs the late-segment plateau 5–15% of write calls (G51 8.5%, no CI)
constants.meaning: The context window carries the call-scale information; memory does not recover it. | Quote the reference window with any erasure or cap cost (H44 round 2).

constants.name: first-nudge activity response
constants.value: 1.16 [0.75, 1.57] active min / 30 min
constants.meaning: A nudge buys about one active minute, a glance, not committed work.

constants.name: information per nudge
constants.value: 1.42 bits
constants.meaning: The nudger uses its information inefficiently.

constants.name: human reply premium
constants.meaning: Status-weighted attention, not deference.

constants.name: kickoff quench target recovery
constants.value: 18/33 periods (p 3e−6) | updated 2026-10-05 (H54 round 2): gte 20/33 (bge 18/33), median π 1.0 in both; per-period π Spearman 0.75 across models, verdicts agree in 29/33
constants.meaning: Day-1 content lands on what the kickoff names.

constants.name: re-allocation speed-limit slack, named-target kickoff
constants.value: 1.00–1.40 (settling 0.25–0.5 active h); free choice 5–15
constants.meaning: A named target moves agents at the speed limit: each moved agent switches once.

constants.name: day-edge share of excess irreversibility
constants.scope: first and last 30 min vs 12–25% time share
constants.meaning: The scheduler's day end carries the swarm's excess entropy production.

constants.name: agent-constant share of systematic style variance
constants.value: 0.55 (F3 three-component share 0.72, IQR 0.65–0.80; context fill 0.08; per-message systematic share κ 0.27)
constants.meaning: Style is mostly a fixed property of the agent; context and role add little.

constants.name: reply premium for idea adoption
constants.scope: 23/26 periods; a thread field alone gives ≈ 3
constants.meaning: Reply partners adopt ideas more than room-mates, but much of it is shared thread context, not copying.

constants.name: P(new idea reaches a 2nd agent within 24 h)
constants.value: median 0.15; seed-length effect −0.26 ± 0.04 std log-odds
constants.meaning: Most new ideas die; long, item-dense seed messages spread each item less.

constants.name: between-agent SD of the dilution exponent
constants.value: 0.09–0.20 (median ≈ 0.15); cross-period ICC 0.23
constants.meaning: Dilution is one exponent per period; agents scatter narrowly around it.

constants.name: restatement source-in-context enrichment
constants.value: 3.38 [2.56, 4.46]; loop exit per forced erasure ×2.40 [1.18, 4.88] | updated 2026-10-05 (H69 round 2): erasure acts as a step, not a dose: exit × own tokens removed OR 1.26 [0.95, 1.69] per log unit (a 2-fold dose excluded, power 1.00); exit OR at the mean dose 2.49 [1.14, 5.44]; post hoc, exit ×3.74 [1.83, 7.61] when the looping text is not in memory (interaction 0.42 [0.26, 0.68])
constants.meaning: Loops are copies of what is still in the context window; erasure breaks them. | Ending a restatement loop is not an output gain: H44 round 2 finds that most flagged (command) loops are productive and a reset costs a looping agent output (E_loop).

constants.name: idle-gate trap aging (sustained escape)
constants.meaning: Escape gets harder the longer an agent idles; recent chatter makes it harder still.

constants.name: assigned antagonism at prize settlement
constants.meaning: Antagonism tracks an open prize and stops within minutes of the verdict.

constants.name: cross-agent call-turnaround co-movement
constants.meaning: A shared latency field appears only in large swarms and tracks load (congestion).

constants.name: schema-diff change-detector false-alarm rate
constants.value: 0/34 placebo days (Wilson upper ≈ 0.10); fused detector 0.18
constants.meaning: Diffing the raw record's schema catches platform changes with no false alarms.

constants.name: value of the context window per bit (Kolchinsky κ)
constants.value: 5.2 [3.8, 8.4] (H70); 5.2 [3.8, 7.9] on an independent mapping (H87) commits per 20 calls per bit; artifact κ_A −0.6 [−1.6, +0.3]; memory, chat reads, search, human messages not identified (I < 0.05 bits)
constants.meaning: Only the context window carries output value; artifacts carry location, not output.

constants.name: memory-size reversion per compression cycle
constants.value: 0.67 [0.63, 0.71] (regime III 0.77; relaxation ≈ 3.8 cycles ≈ 55 active min)
constants.meaning: Memory size is regulated around an agent set point, with no overshoot.

constants.name: read-out loop gain of talk (hop 1)
constants.value: regime III median 0.13 (#51 0.142 [0.111, 0.174]); regime I 0.005; max upper bound 0.39 | updated 2026-10-05 (H67 round 2): agrees with the Fano-implied total gain g_Fano 0.149 [0.123, 0.175] (25 regime-III units; pool 0.127); H50's twice-larger value is its estimator; regime I on the chat clock g_chat −0.022 [−0.052, 0.009]
constants.meaning: One message causes about 0.13 extra messages through reading; the swarm is far from runaway.

constants.name: chat link before a herding burst
constants.value: 60% vs 12% of controls (OR 11.9 [9.2, 15.3]); deploys 2.2% vs 1.8%
constants.meaning: Pile-ons are announced in chat; commits and deploys follow them.

constants.name: shared-field gauge (pair covariance)
constants.value: raw 0.016, trimmed 0.008 (regime III 0.013 → 0.005); shared share φ trimmed 0.04 (regime III); talk φ 0.21
constants.meaning: The share of activity variance shared across agents; trimming the schedule removes most of it.

constants.name: talk scaling with N
constants.value: 0.33 [−0.18, 0.64] (regime I 0.09, III 0.77); addressing per message slope 0.79 [0.41, 1.39]
constants.meaning: More agents do not mean proportionally more talk; each message addresses more.

constants.name: Price transmission share of within-period culture change
constants.value: content 0.98 (IQR 0.95–1.00); style 0.95; conventions 0.98; migration 0.004 (style 0.044); selection ≤ 0.03
constants.meaning: Culture changes because stayers change, not through turnover or differential influence; there is no persistent attractor.

constants.name: collective talk entropy production through named partners
constants.value: 7.6 [4.3, 11.2]×10⁻³ nats/min (0.017 nats per agent-hour); unnamed ≈ 0; behavior collective share 0.003
constants.meaning: The only collective arrow of time runs through who names whom.

constants.name: re-allocation slack by goal type
constants.value: assigned artifact: S 1.0–2.5, settling 0.25–0.75 active h; open goal: S 3.0–14.5, 4–13 h
constants.meaning: A concrete artifact in the goal settles the swarm in under an hour.

constants.name: village-culture slow-mode decay time (regime I)
constants.value: 28 ± 5 d (bge), 23 ± 4 d (gte); within #51 common mode ≈ 3 active days; round 2: joint OU τ with H82 20.9 ± 2.8 / 15.5 ± 2.2 d (regime I); τ_u 2.4 / 1.7 goal periods (84 / 57 documented h); regime III block τ 9.7 / 6.8 d, boundary 6.5 d; post hoc (H106): the regime-I amplitude sits in the N < 8 era (#2–#19, near-lag similarity 0.25/0.28 vs 0.11/0.00 for #20–#31); #51 common-mode lag-1 survival φ 0.54 (τ ≈ 1.6 active days)
constants.scope: 24 regime-I goals; absent in regime III
constants.meaning: A collective content mode beyond the members persists for weeks in chat-mode swarms (an external-drift rival is open).

constants.name: day-1 previous-period carry-over
constants.value: 0.158 / 0.153 (bge/gte), no decay over days 1–5; absorbed by the agent's own previous content
constants.meaning: Agents carry their own old content into a new goal; the village record adds nothing beyond that.

constants.name: daily rotation of content collective modes
constants.value: median z_boot 1.0 (stationary null 0.1–0.75); clip forecast gain 0.10 [0.03, 0.16]; forecastable share content ≈ 0.30, talk ≤ 0.05, activity ≈ 0
constants.meaning: Collective content modes drift slowly every day; the persistent structure is one uniform mode.

constants.name: spontaneous share of the room content split
constants.value: f_spont 0.58–0.91 (5/7 regime-III periods significant); f_comp 0.03–0.18; Q_spont 1.8–4.2 with identical kickoffs, Q 5–7 with room-specific kickoffs
constants.meaning: Rooms diverge in content mostly on their own within a goal; the residual may still hold unmeasured room-specific work fields.

constants.name: room content bimodality
constants.value: D 5.3–6.1 when rooms do different work (#38, #41, #44, #51g); median 1.7 with identical kickoffs
constants.meaning: Two content domains form when the rooms do different work; there is no wall between them: content follows the room an agent speaks in.

constants.name: cross-room read dose on home content
constants.value: |κ_R| < 0.04 per e-fold of hopping read-outs (−0.014 [−0.042, 0.024]); power ≥ 0.93 at 0.1
constants.meaning: Reading the other room does not carry its content home.

constants.name: agent content-constant variance
constants.value: τ² ≈ 0.0014 per coordinate (reliability across periods r 0.49 bge, 0.45 gte); day noise σ² ≈ 0.0035
constants.meaning: Agents carry a real but small personal content offset across periods.

constants.name: mover adoption time
constants.value: ≤ 1 day (φ 0.88 on day 1; single mover, Gemini 3.1 Pro 05-25); one mover kept its old side (GPT-5.4 04-27)
constants.meaning: A moved agent usually takes on its new room's content within a day; not universal.

constants.name: chat gain after an erasure
constants.value: +22% [8, 36] output beyond the placebo-call effect; ≈ 0 allocation bits
constants.meaning: Chat helps a freshly erased agent restart work without carrying where-to-work information; a candidate lever, not yet tested as one.

constants.name: history-search outage cost
constants.value: β +0.12 per search per 100 calls (dip ≥ 0.30 excluded); commits +0.03 ± 0.51
constants.meaning: Losing history search for two days had no measured cost.

constants.name: single-agent talk memory per minute
constants.value: median 0.006 over 70 units (talk); activity ≈ 0.25, #51 0.34
constants.meaning: Talk minutes carry no single-agent memory; relaxation must be measured on the per-call clock.

constants.name: collective talk memory excess over mean-field Glauber
constants.value: period median +0.077; #51 +0.067 [0.034, 0.100]; content Δg₁ median −0.17 (content acts as a field); round 2 W0-corrected after scheduler removal (V5): median +0.052, #51 +0.042 [0.014, 0.070]; 92% of lag-1 covariance within rooms (Π ≈ 15)
constants.meaning: The collective memory is read-out coupling within rooms, matching H67's hop-1 gain; not a slow common drive.

constants.name: nudge response over the Onsager-regression prediction
constants.value: WITHDRAWN (H99 round 2): the ×9.5 ratio did not survive the corrected masks; nudge talk-per-call Ω 1.7 [0.8, 2.7], human-message Ω 2.5 [1.6, 3.4] (post hoc)
constants.meaning: Kicks do not clearly outlive the fluctuation clock once masks and centring are fixed.

constants.name: pairwise sufficiency of convention co-usage (fields removed)
constants.value: median 0.91 (regime I 0.89, III 0.93); raw I₂/I_N 0.95; field share φ 0.71 (I) / 0.26 (III); remainder 3–5% of I_N
constants.meaning: Pairwise couplings plus fields explain co-usage; in regime III pairwise structure dominates.

constants.name: co-usage coupling within vs across teams
constants.value: +0.15 within vs −0.60 across (p 0.0005)
constants.meaning: Assigned teams show up as antiferromagnetic co-usage blocks across team lines.

constants.name: kickoff extra forgetting of agent content positions
constants.value: +0.26 ± 0.04 (16/18 kickoffs); ordinary-day memory ρ0 ≈ 0.62 (regime I), 0.83 (III); ρ at kickoff ≈ 0.4; along kickoff 0.63 vs transverse 0.25; day-1 overshoot a +0.12 ± 0.02
constants.meaning: A new goal is an anisotropic restoring force that erases most of the previous content position, with day-1 overshoot.

constants.name: on-goal occupancy after a kickoff
constants.value: decoy floor ≈ 0.03 → 0.23–0.44 in assigned weeks (always < ½); #51 own-goal ≈ 0.27 steady over 9 weeks; #12a two-state loop gain g₂ 0.10 → 0.74
constants.meaning: Goal adoption is a rising on-goal share with binomial spread; most statements stay off the literal goal.

constants.name: project-choice share coefficient (not identified as coupling)
constants.meaning: No period is bistable; repo bursts mimic the share term, and habit dominates.

constants.name: ownership price in max-ent work allocation
constants.value: median 2.2 nats shared weeks (1.2–3.3) vs 7.8 own-role (4.8–20); D₁ 0.3–1.9 vs 2.7–4.1 bits per quantum; residual ≤ 0.13·D₁ in 23/24 units; κ on episodes 1.35–4.1 shared
constants.meaning: Work allocation is max-ent given activity, repo size, ownership and rooms; ownership is the goal-set price.

constants.name: mean-field amplification bound
constants.value: χ = 1/(1 − g_lag) ≤ 1.31 in every unit; observables vary ×3 (herding, branching), ×13 (loops), ×127 (settling) across periods
constants.meaning: Coupling amplifies at most ~30%, too little to organize the phase diagram; regime and N do the work.

constants.name: content disorder ratio (random field share)
constants.value: #51 0.67–0.73 vs shared-goal weeks 0.24–0.53 (style-residualized; raw contrast weeks 0.74–0.79); role text explains 5–14%; mean-field gain b_MF 0.23–0.31 (J ≲ 0.2)
constants.meaning: Private goals make a static random field; shared-goal disorder is mostly style.

constants.name: human-step switch response
constants.value: #51 ×1.07–1.09 (upper ×1.18–1.32); between-step dispersion D 1.12–1.18; kickoff ratio K 1.2–4.0 (48–100% of agents switch in the first 2 h on kickoff days vs 17–86%)
constants.meaning: Human messages do not trigger avalanches; kickoffs do.

constants.name: newcomer day-1 own-role percentile
constants.value: 0.57 vs incumbents 0.83
constants.meaning: Late joiners start off their role and take time to align.

constants.name: collective attention decay of a finished period
constants.value: terms τ 5.5 village days (median, 20 periods) to a floor of 1.9%; artifacts τ ≈ 4, floor ≈ 0; veterans' days 21–40 share 0.079 of days 1–3; biexponential (τ₁ ≈ 2, τ₂ ≈ 48 d) wins 5/27 fits
constants.meaning: The village forgets a finished goal within about a week; the floor is fed partly by re-coinage.

constants.name: newcomer content gap to veterans
constants.value: −0.020 [−0.056, +0.020] at tenure days 2–4, ≈ 0 by days 8–14; family signature at entry K_E +0.038 (13/15), fades by 0.018; own-room alignment 0.18 (veterans 0.16); newcomer/veteran use of just-finished terms 0.93
constants.meaning: Newcomers fit in within a day or two.

constants.name: veterans' persistent shared content fraction
constants.value: ≈ 3% of statement variance within a period, 0.5% across periods (bge, style-residualized, kickoff-projected)
constants.meaning: There is little persistent village culture in content; culture tests on window means have little power.

constants.name: day-1 old-state persistence after a goal switch
constants.value: 0.18–0.27 vs 0.85–0.89 across an ordinary night (24 transitions, both models); inertia τ_old ≈ 0.15 active h; residual switching time τ_sw median 7–15 active h
constants.meaning: A goal switch is a quench that erases most of the old state on day 1.

constants.name: night factor in content remanence decay
constants.value: λ 0.83–1.06 (no night step); β_N ≈ 0 ± 0.02; weekend β_G ≈ −0.015 per extra 24 h; own idle gap β_gap ≈ +0.10; context reset β_R ≈ 0; overnight re-orientation toward the goal +0.03
constants.meaning: Content memory decays with active work, not with nights; mornings slightly re-orient agents to the goal.

constants.name: room-split onset ratio (day 1 over final)
constants.value: #37 0.09, #39 −0.09 (grows from zero); #41 0.71, #42 0.89 (near full on day 1); day-1 direction kept c₁ ≈ 0.5 (#44 0.84)
constants.meaning: Room splits sometimes grow from zero and sometimes appear at once; the kickoff day's direction is only half kept.

constants.name: rotational diffusion of the room-difference direction
constants.value: P(1) pooled 0.70 identical-kickoff vs 0.93 fielded; D_θ 0.35 vs 0.075 per day; #38 plateau P(ℓ) ≈ 0.85
constants.meaning: The room direction persists within a period, more under a room field; size and field are confounded.

constants.name: room-alignment drop at a forced erasure
constants.value: −0.08 [−0.23, 0.07] bge, −0.07 gte (3,477 erasures); read pull κ_R 0.019 [0.003, 0.034] per e-fold of room items read; median 2 statements per reset segment
constants.meaning: Room order is not stored in the context window.

constants.name: own-repo pinned day-1 residual
constants.value: 0.30 [−0.01, 0.57] bge (0.22 gte); 0.11 by day 2; not commit-locked
constants.meaning: An agent's own repo barely anchors it to an old goal.

constants.name: talk Fano sum-rule ratio (observed / 1/(1 − g_lag)²)
constants.value: regime III 1.01 [0.94, 1.09] (18 units, τ² 0); regime I 1.34 [1.18, 1.52]; median Φ(10 min) 1.32 / 1.92 / 1.29 (I / II / III); cross-room covariance 0 in 0/12 two-room units | updated 2026-10-05 (H67 round 2): regime-I r_F with the chat-clock gain g_I 1.35 [1.14, 1.60], unchanged: the regime-I excess is not chat-clock read-out coupling; r_F with the multi-hop G₅ 0.78 [0.67, 0.90] (descriptive)
constants.meaning: In regime III the collective talk variance is exactly what the read-out gain predicts; regime I has a fast extra field or coupling.

constants.name: reply thread momentum
constants.value: h(1) − g_rep +0.16 (54/54 units); g_rep medians 0.36 (I) / 0.53 (III); strong reply pairs 37 directed in 18/66 units
constants.meaning: Replies beget replies within a thread; no Griffiths phase from rare strong pairs.

constants.name: room-gated read-out gain on the call clock
constants.value: 0.113 [0.077, 0.149] (regime III); per read named message +0.073 [0.063, 0.084], unnamed +0.0017; named one call later +0.025
constants.meaning: Named messages couple at the next call (and weakly one call later); unnamed messages barely do.

constants.name: negative in-flight field
constants.value: −0.0084 per message in flight near a call; −0.0048 cross-room in flight
constants.meaning: Unreadable messages near a call lower talk (turn-taking or API contention); in-flight-gated gains overstate coupling ~×2.

constants.name: true disagreement rate on the merits (validated stance flag)
constants.value: #12 opposite teams 0.52 [0.33, 0.82] (#12 noise) to 0.76 [0.47, 1.0] (population noise); teammates ≤ 0.05–0.08; unassigned #33 0.019, #26 0.007, #40 0.042; post-verdict 0 flags in 90 replies; #51 flag rate 0.85% (rivals +0.46 [−1.46, 1.37] log-odds vs unrelated)
constants.meaning: Real disagreement needs assigned sides and ends at the verdict; without sides it stays at 1–2%.

constants.name: debate talk couplings per call (Ising units)
constants.value: #12 opposite team J_OT 0.20 ± 0.05, same team J_ST 0.04 ± 0.06; judge-sink bound < 0.6; election out-coupling step +0.09 ± 0.33; minimum detectable single-event step ≈ 0.6–0.75 (80% power, 10 agents, 83 min)
constants.meaning: Debaters answer opponents; leadership roles do not raise call-level talk influence.

constants.name: per-agent read-out pull of a human message
constants.value: 0.090 [0.071, 0.109] (bge) / 0.088 [0.069, 0.107] (gte), 181 messages, 990 read pairs; post hoc: 0.22 ± 0.02 (SE) when the first post-read message is < 30 s, ≈ 0 by 10 min
constants.scope: human messages ≥ 250 characters, not kickoffs; regimes I and III; first post-read chat message, decoy-corrected
constants.meaning: Each reader moves toward a human message at its first post-read message; half the pull is gone within about a minute (decay profile post hoc).

constants.name: read minus in-flight re-quench at matched lag and before-age
constants.value: +0.11 [0.05, 0.17] (bge) / +0.12 [0.07, 0.18] (gte); 93 in-flight pairs, 72 messages; matched read 0.21 vs in flight 0.10
constants.scope: human messages; regime I carries the contrast (regime III 13 in-flight pairs)
constants.meaning: Reading adds to the pull beyond contemporaneous convergence; convergence is 40–50% of the matched pull (f_conv).

constants.name: erasure dose slope of restatement-loop exit
constants.scope: G38, G40, G41, G51 pooled (all labs); upper bound: a weak dose ≤ 0.53 is not excluded
constants.meaning: Every full erasure removes the copied source, so loop exit is a step, not proportional to how much is erased.

constants.name: own tool tokens as a loop-onset trigger
constants.scope: G38, G51; all-lab token sample (drops many OpenAI and DeepSeek statements)
constants.meaning: Own tool output does not raise restatement onset; trimming tool output does not prevent loops.

constants.name: memory share of erasure-crossing restatements
constants.scope: regime III, word 3-gram containment ≥ 0.5; pooled claim failed as frozen
constants.meaning: In #51 most loops that survive an erasure restate the agent's memory; elsewhere memory plays no detectable role. Carriage and salience are not separable.

constants.name: memory moderation of erasure loop exit (post hoc)
constants.value: 0.42 [0.26, 0.68] (I² 0); erasure exit ×3.74 [1.83, 7.61] when the looping text is not in memory
constants.scope: G38, G39, G40, G51; post hoc, needs a fresh test (H69-R4)
constants.meaning: An erasure breaks a loop less when the looping content is in memory: check memory before relying on a reset.

constants.name: forced-erasure style displacement percentile (genre and position removed)
constants.value: 0.546 [0.522, 0.564] (5,673 forced pairs, 23 units); genre-matched strata 0.545; content 0.513 (bge) / 0.510 (gte), CIs include ½; round-1 0.564 → 0.547 after agent-scale fix
constants.scope: regime III, NE41, scaled pairs, agent-cluster CI; 18/23 units
constants.meaning: Exogenous erasures move style, not content, beyond speech-act genre.

constants.name: context-held style offset share
constants.value: ≈ 0.046 [0.017, 0.072] of per-message style variance (ΔC(1) 0.70 [0.26, 1.11]); flat in lag 1–4, 0.64 already at the first post-reset message (post hoc)
constants.scope: regime III, gap-matched, clipped units, agent bootstrap (approximate)
constants.meaning: A forced erasure redraws a per-segment style offset; no OU drift grows with position (kill fired).

constants.name: drop in style self-pull across a forced erasure
constants.value: 0.145 [0.086, 0.184] (ρ in context 0.36 [0.27, 0.45] → after erasure 0.22 [0.16, 0.27]); room-register term 0.11 does not absorb it
constants.scope: regime III, own last ≤ 3 messages, gap-matched
constants.meaning: An agent imitates its own in-context style; erasing the context removes part of that pull.

constants.name: agent identification across goal switches (function words + style)
constants.value: 0.85 (chance 0.15); style 0.77, function words 0.79, content 0.51
constants.meaning: 50 function-word rates plus 17 formatting rates attribute messages to an agent across a goal switch; embeddings do not.

constants.name: content read-out jump (matched age, hop 1)
constants.scope: regime III, 16 units (CI > 0 in 10, < 0 in none); whitened cosine with a same-sender placebo
constants.meaning: Content couples at the recipient's read-out call, as talk does, mostly through named messages. H08 r2: without names or replies in the response, no read-out content effect is found (different estimand).

constants.name: relay read-out jump at a third agent (post hoc)
constants.scope: regime III, 27 units, start-time RD at C-hops ≥ 2; post hoc estimator; not valid in regime I
constants.meaning: A relay couples a third agent only when it names it.

constants.name: batched relay read share
constants.value: 0.60 (regime III), 0.41 (regime I); ρ = 2 in 19% / 33%
constants.scope: relay pairs (source and relay read by a third agent)
constants.meaning: Path length 2 often collapses into one read-out call: the third agent reads the source and the relay together.

constants.name: regime-I read → chat-mode switch
constants.value: 0.024 [0.019, 0.029] at hop 1 (0.026–0.041 to hop 6), ≈ 70% of the regime-I talk jump; chat-mode recipients k₁ 0.110 [0.087, 0.133] vs computer use 0.005 (post hoc split); H67 r2: ≈ 3/4 is the chat-turn schedule (skeleton null), mode-free excess 0.035 [0.023, 0.046]
constants.scope: regime I; chat-mode calls talk 0.78, computer-use 0.04
constants.meaning: Regime-I talk coupling is mostly a mode switch, and most of that switch is the scaffold's chat-turn order, not coupling.

constants.name: regime-I hop-1 talk jump on logged-start recipients
constants.meaning: The regime-I hop-1 jump is not a latency artifact; the round-1 'continuing rise' is withdrawn.

constants.name: read − in-flight content response at matched lag
constants.value: all statements +1.25 [+0.98, +1.60] cos×100; statements that neither name nor reply to the sender −0.39 [−0.62, −0.12]; CI > 0 for all statements in 3/9 (bge) and 5/9 (gte) regime-III periods
constants.scope: G51, bge, lag × density strata, 1-h block bootstrap
constants.meaning: Read-gated content lives inside addressed replies; without names and replies, co-response wins (κ_c > 1).

constants.name: memory dose rate at forced erasures
constants.scope: regime III, 9 periods; share of forced erasures where the engaged sender is newly written to memory
constants.meaning: Agents write the senders they engage with into memory at most consolidations.

constants.name: memory-salience reply premium
constants.value: +5.5 ± 1.0 pp (SE), CI > 0 in 7/9; protection CF × dose −0.36 ± 0.55 pp (power 0.04 at π = 0.5)
constants.scope: regime III, 9 periods, reply author, LPM with dose × age
constants.meaning: Memory records engagement; whether a name in memory protects a thread across an erasure is unpowered.

constants.name: decoupled-feed episode length
constants.value: 9 days, 17.3 active h, 130 fetches (2026-03-17 17:22 → 03-27 19:29 UTC); 97.7% of fetches stale vs 0.15% before
constants.scope: one episode, the Claude Code agent's event feed; status block stayed current
constants.meaning: A stale feed can decouple one agent silently for days while its goal and day number stay current.

constants.name: event-age monitor detection delay
constants.value: 0.38 active h (2 fetches), 0 false alarms
constants.scope: one episode; alarm when the median event age over the last 5 fetches exceeds 1 h
constants.meaning: A five-fetch event-age monitor catches a replayed feed fast; a content-only monitor does not.

constants.name: 200-event cap omission share
constants.value: 0.0365 of 930,422 received agent messages (G51); 0 in every period before 2026-06-11
constants.meaning: The NE22 cap drops about 4% of #51 messages and nothing earlier.

constants.name: reply-given-talk span elasticity
constants.value: −0.11 [−0.16, −0.06] (τ 0, Q 0.58); synthetic attenuation ≈ 10%
constants.scope: regime III, G38, G40, G41, G44, DQ2 parents
constants.meaning: A talk call answers a pending message almost regardless of its previous call's wall span (doubling the span lowers the hazard 7%). The talk split conditions on talk, which a message can cause.

constants.name: talk-propensity span elasticity
constants.meaning: Long tool calls are followed by fewer talk calls in some periods; this explains about 3/4 of the negative total η and all of its between-period spread.

constants.name: regime-I scheduler-wait elasticity
constants.scope: regime I, Gemini logged chat calls, #24–#31 pooled (274 replies)
constants.meaning: Full-strength wall-clock exposure through the scheduler's wait is excluded; the cause of regime I's η is open.

constants.name: thrash index on blind-checked labels
constants.value: +0.106 [0.089, 0.122] (9/9); conservative (mid-segment label rates) +0.072 [0.067, 0.078]; round-1 classifier +0.079
constants.scope: regime III, 9 non-reserved periods; 300 blind labels, re-acquisition κ 0.87 (single rater)
constants.meaning: A forced wipe raises re-reading; the round-1 value is not a classifier artifact.

constants.name: two-timescale erasure relaxation
constants.value: re-read spike 1 call, tail 8.2 [5.8, 11.8] calls (G51; ΔAIC +104); slow write recovery 8.5 [5.9, 11.1] calls pooled; no residual linear ramp (G51 +0.0002 [−0.0002, 0.0005] per call)
constants.scope: regime III, complete forced sawtooths; tail resolved in G51 and G40 only
constants.meaning: The wipe is a quench with a one-call spike and an ~8-call relaxation; round 1's 'segment-long ramp' is the end of this relaxation.

constants.name: cap output ratio
constants.scope: regime III, 9 periods; also per wall-clock minute; optimum beyond 40 not identified
constants.meaning: Halving the context cap from 40 to 20 calls costs about 12% of output per call.

constants.name: post-reset re-open share of the erased working set
constants.value: forced 0.60 [0.53, 0.67] vs no reset 0.66 [0.57, 0.75]; recency-adjusted excess −0.039 [−0.085, +0.007]; forced − voluntary +0.040 [0.017, 0.062]
constants.scope: regime III, file-path objects, last 20 pre-wipe calls
constants.meaning: Agents re-read their working set by habit, not the erased files in particular; the wipe raises the volume of re-reading, not its targeting.

constants.name: output effect of a reset on a looping agent
constants.value: −0.086 [−0.151, −0.022] writes per call over 10 calls (6 periods; G51 −0.073); post hoc: stuck loops (no writes) +0.011 [−0.015, 0.037], productive loops −0.149 [−0.201, −0.097]
constants.scope: regime III, command-hash loop flag (≥ 3 in-loop calls in the 10 calls before)
constants.meaning: A forced reset does not pay as a loop breaker: most flagged loops are productive repetition.

constants.name: Fano-implied total talk gain
constants.scope: regime III, 25 units; H111's Φ(10) inverted with no refit; upper bound on the read-out gain
constants.meaning: The fluctuation side agrees with the response side (g_lag 0.127) and excludes H50's 0.24; hops 2–5 add at most ≈ 0.05.

constants.name: regime-I chat-clock read-out gain
constants.meaning: On the talk-capable calls, a fresh read does not raise talk beyond messages in flight.

constants.name: regime-I read-out gain without call-mode conditioning (post hoc)
constants.value: 0.035 [0.023, 0.046] (0.056 raw minus skeleton null 0.019)
constants.scope: regime I, 38 units, skeleton-null corrected; post hoc
constants.meaning: A small regime-I coupling that call-class cells hide; far below the g ≈ 0.13 that H111's regime-I excess would need.

constants.name: first stage at the read-out boundary
constants.value: 1.04 (regime III median); 0.95 (regime I)
constants.meaning: One read per message crosses the boundary, so per-read normalization does not cause the H50/H67 gap.
